slides.title: Gita on *anger, greed* & desire
slides.sub: You cleaned the whole house for Diwali. Krishna says 3 things inside you need cleaning too.

slides.deva: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
slides.iast: tri-vidhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ, kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṃ tyajet
slides.meaning: Desire, anger and greed are three doors to hell. They ruin a person. So give up all three.

slides.title: Three *doors*, not three monsters
slides.body: Krishna tells Arjuna: kama is wanting more, krodha is anger, lobha is greed. Each looks small. Each one lets trouble walk in.

slides.title: The *want-more* door
slides.body: 11:58 p.m. The Diwali sale ends in 2 minutes. Your cart is full of things you didn't want an hour ago. Try it: wait 24 hours, then buy.

slides.title: The *anger* door
slides.body: Guests come at 7. The house is a mess. You snap at Mummy. Try it: before you reply, drink a glass of water. Then talk.

slides.title: The *greed* door
slides.body: Who got the bigger Diwali gift? Who paid less for the sweets? Greed keeps score. Try it: this week, give something and don't count it.

slides.title: Screenshot this: *the 3-door check*
slides.body: Before you buy, reply or grab, ask: Am I wanting? Am I angry? Am I counting? If yes, wait one day.

slides.title: Which *door* is open in your house?
slides.sub: Save this for the next Diwali sale, and send it to the family member who snaps first during cleaning. Follow @sutraverselife for real-life lessons from ancient wisdom.
